strategy.summary: Trade the spread between ES and NQ: long one leg, short the other, betting the gap snaps back. The hedge ratio comes from Ning & Lee (Purdue Statistics, 2024): instead of a regression, pick the ratio that makes the spread revert to its mean FASTEST (the empirical mean-reversion time, EMRT). The paper used daily stock pairs; everything here is intraday futures, so it is an extrapolation. Two plain ratios run alongside as controls: the OLS regression slope and 1:1 dollar-neutral. If EMRT doesn't beat them, it adds nothing.
strategy.formula: spread = (ES move ÷ ES price) − β × (NQ move ÷ NQ price); β = argmin EMRT

rules.label: Hedge
rules.text: At each month start, fit β on the previous 3, 6 or 12 months only. EMRT: mark every swing of at least C × the spread's sd (an 'important extremum'), time how long each takes to get back to the mean, and pick the β from 0.20 to 3.00 with the shortest average (C = 1.5, 2.0 or 2.5), as long as the spread's variance is at most 2× the OLS spread's. Controls: OLS slope; β = 1.

rules.label: Enter
rules.text: z = the spread against the formation window's mean and sd, or a rolling 50, 100 or 250-bar window. A fresh cross below −entry buys the spread (long ES, short β × NQ); above +entry sells it. Both legs fill at the next bar's open. No entries in the last 30 minutes; a signal while a position is open is dropped.

rules.label: Exit
rules.text: Close when z gets back to 0 (at mean) or half-way to it; optional stop once z runs a further 1.5 or 2.5 past the entry level; optional time stop after 3 × the spread's EMRT. Either flat at the session's last close, or held across sessions (a contract roll while held costs a round turn). The open position keeps its entry month's hedge.

rules.label: Size
rules.text: Both / long spread / short spread; one position at a time. Whole ES and NQ contracts, the two legs' full contract value together no more than the account (no leverage), starting from $10,000,000 so the ratio is carried by tens of contracts.

strategy.length_note: Formation is in months; z windows, EMRT and time stops are in bars of the chosen bar size.

funnel.name: Start
funnel.why: All 51,840 versions backtested once on 2018–2022 data.

funnel.name: 1 · Integrity
funnel.why: Per-trade checks on every version: the spread's z was recomputed by a separate route, each hedge was fit only on months before the trade, each entry was a fresh cross on an allowed side, no qualifying signal was skipped while flat, both legs filled at the next open no better than the market, exits fired at the first bar a rule did, and P&L, roll costs and sizing add up. Plus 40 random versions re-run on cut-off data. 0 failed.

funnel.name: 2 · Enough trades
funnel.why: Needs ≥100 completed trades and ≥10 a year in ≥4 of the 5 years. Removed 31,439 (7,374 on 15min, 10,491 on 30min, 13,574 on 1h).

funnel.name: 3 · Profit
funnel.why: Needs a net profit, Sharpe ≥ 0.75 and drawdown no worse than 30%. Removed 20,369 (9,884 on 15min, 6,782 on 30min, 3,703 on 1h); 17,502 of them lost money.

funnel.name: 4 · Stable settings
funnel.why: Each setting is nudged one at a time, down and up: the formation window and a rolling z window by ±20% (rounded, at least one month / bar), the entry |z| by ±0.25, a stop by ±0.25 z, an EMRT hedge's C by ±0.25 and a time stop by ±0.5 × EMRT ("none" has nothing to nudge). At least 70% of the nudged versions must be profitable, with median Sharpe ≥ 0.5. Removed 9.

funnel.name: 6 · Remove duplicates
funnel.why: Versions whose monthly returns correlate ≥ 0.8 form a group; the best 2 of each go on (a group of one keeps its one). 23 versions formed 9 groups; 14 of the 16 picks are distinct backtests.

funnel.name: 8 · Validation
funnel.why: Frozen finalists run once on unseen data: needs net > 0, Sharpe ≥ 0.3, drawdown no worse than 30% and ≥40 trades. Not run yet: the finalists are frozen and waiting for this step.

assumptions: Data: Databento CME continuous front month (ES.v.0 and NQ.v.0), 1-minute bars aggregated to 15 minutes, 30 minutes and 1 hour and joined on bar time (a bar missing in either leg is dropped from both). Rolls are back-adjusted per leg; the spread uses only real point moves scaled by real prices.
Day session only: NYSE regular session 09:30-16:00 NY for both legs, on NYSE trading days.
Costs on EACH leg: 1 tick slippage per side (stops too) and $2.50 commission per contract per side; holding over a roll costs that leg a round turn.

Unlevered across both legs, so returns are small next to a single-market strategy; a market-neutral book would normally run levered. Sharpe doesn't depend on that choice; return and drawdown scale with it.
The paper tested daily stock pairs with a reinforcement-learning trader. Here a plain z band trades the spread on intraday futures bars, so the whole grid is an extrapolation of the paper.
Decisions use both legs' bar closes and fill at the next bar's open on both legs.
Sharpe uses daily mark-to-market returns (√252) of both legs, with idle cash earning 0%. Time in market is the share of bars with an open position.
Benchmark row: holding ES alone, for scale; the spread is roughly market-neutral and not trying to beat it.
Other strategy families were already selected on these legs' 2023–2024 data, so 2023–2024 is not untouched; only the 2025+ holdout is (and single-market picks were already scored on it).
Holdout (2025 onward) has not been run. It is a one-time final test and needs an explicit go-ahead.
